title: Cardiac MRI
what: Images of the heart in a magnetic field. They show the muscle, valves, chambers, and how the heart pumps. No radiation.
why: For cardiomyopathy, after myocarditis or a heart attack, for heart defects from birth, or when a heart ultrasound gave no clear answer.
duration: usually 45 to 60 minutes; the report in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: A pacemaker, defibrillator, or other implant with electronics
Metal in your body: joint replacements, plates, clips on blood vessels, or shrapnel
If you are or might be pregnant
If you are afraid of closed spaces. Your doctor will suggest ways to help
If your pulse is irregular. The scan will take longer
Kidney disease, or allergy to contrast dye

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light meal is usually fine. If there will be a stress test with medicine, special rules apply. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Coffee
prepare.text: If a stress test is ordered, coffee, tea, and chocolate are usually cut out for 24 hours before.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off everything metal: jewelry, watches, hair clips, piercings. Leave your phone and cards in the locker.

bring: Heart ultrasound, ECGs, and cardiologist reports
steps: An IV line is put in a vein
ECG stickers are put on your chest
You lie on your back, and a coil is placed on your chest
You are asked many times to hold your breath for 10 to 15 seconds
The machine knocks loudly. You get headphones
Halfway through, contrast is given and more images are taken
feel: It does not hurt, but it is loud and tight
Holding your breath is tiring. You can ask for a break
With contrast: a cool feeling in the vein
after: You can go back to your day right away
After contrast, drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
Take the report to a cardiologist
red_flags: Pressing chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting: call emergency services right away
After contrast: itching, a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Why does it take so long?
faq.a: The heart moves, so images are timed to your heartbeat and breathing. Many series are needed.

faq.q: Can I have a cardiac MRI with a pacemaker?
faq.a: Only if it is MRI-safe and your cardiologist approves. Tell staff in advance.

reminders.text: Cardiac MRI tomorrow. Bring your heart ultrasound, ECGs, and a list of medicines. Take off everything metal.
